items.title: Testing is the platform default and opt-out is durable and scoped
items.statement: Automated testing and evidence collection remain defaults. Restriction requires a user-approved durable testing_policy_override with exact scope, rationale, authority, evidence, redaction, and lifecycle fields; affected work is labeled as an exception rather than a pass or full certification.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: 'Automated testing and evidence collection are platform defaults for planned and executed work; Planning Wizard conversations refine requirements and constraints but do not casually disable the automated testing system. Disabling or restricting automated testing requires a durable testing_policy_override explicitly approved by the user for exact projects, PlanUnits, WorkNodes, capability classes, reasons, risks, approver_ref, approved_at_utc, evidence_refs, redaction_profile_ref, and expiration or reopen conditions. Affected work remains truthfully marked with an approved verification exception, such as completed_with_approved_verification_exception, and must never be represented as an automated test pass or full certification. Visible or headed-session verification cannot pass without interaction evidence, artifact evidence, and redaction disposition.'

items.builder_discretion: The storage representation is open, but the enumerated override fields and truthful exception semantics are not optional.

items.title: Restricted testing has a truthful exception oracle
items.statement: A Testing Off or restricted-testing record passes acceptance only when it records approver, scope, risk, evidence, redaction profile, lifecycle condition, and a truthful exception result.

evidence.exact_quote: - Testing Off or restricted testing records approver, scope, risk, evidence, redaction profile, expiration or reopen condition, and truthful exception result.

items.title: Casual conversation and unavailable capabilities do not disable testing
items.statement: The system must not solicit testing existence as if opt-out were normal, infer opt-out from casual conversation or unavailable settings, translate exceptions into passes, or permit an evidence-free visible-session pass.

evidence.exact_quote: - Do not ask whether testing should exist as though no testing were the ordinary default.
- Do not infer an opt-out from casual conversation or a capability setting being unavailable.
- Do not convert an approved testing exception into test_passed or certified.
- Do not allow visible-session pass without evidence and redaction disposition.

items.title: Plan Compile performs project and live capability discovery
items.statement: Before WorkNode test bindings are finalized, Plan Compile discovers project-native test infrastructure, while Test Capability Discovery researches current official and primary sources across live, GUI, device, accessibility, performance, security, and related testing methods and records provenance and selection metadata.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: 'Plan Compile performs project-level discovery of existing runners, commands, harnesses, frameworks, environments, services, emulators, browsers, devices, credentials, and evidence surfaces before finalizing WorkNode-specific test bindings. Test Capability Discovery searches current official and primary sources for appropriate live testing, hot reload, live preview, browser automation, GUI automation, simulator, emulator, device, cloud, accessibility, performance, security, and project-native testing methods relevant to the technology stack. Online capability research records source URL or provider reference, publication or update time when available, retrieval time, tool and version, supported platform, license, cost, credential needs, installation scope, freshness, confidence, and selection rationale.'

items.title: Capability research must not rely only on stale model knowledge
items.statement: Current tool, version, setup, and platform claims require more than internal model knowledge; official-source research with provenance is contractually required.

items.title: Authorized tool installation is bounded, receipted, revalidated, and reversible
items.statement: Missing testing support may be installed locally or under pre-authorization. Higher-impact actions require authority and may block. Writes use safe points, bounded surfaces, receipts, revalidation, and rollback.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: 'When an appropriate test, live-preview, hot-reload, browser, simulator, emulator, or support method is missing, the system may install or configure it within project-local or pre-authorized policy and must record commands, changes, receipts, rollback, and currentness. Global or privileged installation, paid services, license acceptance, account creation, credential use, device enrollment, or material external effects require applicable authority and may become a typed blocker rather than an unsafe silent install. Testing-tool installation and configuration writes use FileSafe/source-control safe points, bounded write surfaces, receipts, revalidation, and rollback so discovery cannot damage the user''s project or environment.'

items.title: Testing capability settings inherit and propagate an effective snapshot
items.statement: Each capability family is globally configurable and project-overridable, and the resulting effective policy snapshot propagates to Planning Wizard, Plan Compile, Executor, and Orchestrator.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: 'Testing capability policy is configurable globally and per project, with project settings inheriting or overriding global values and the effective policy snapshot carried into Planning Wizard, Plan Compile, Executor, and Orchestrator. items.title: Visible verification defaults to show_when_possible
items.statement: When a meaningful visual surface exists, the active session is exposed. Web sessions show browser interactions and evidence; native sessions show suitable preview, simulator, device, application, trace, screenshot, and log surfaces when available and permitted.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: 'The default testing visibility policy is show_when_possible: when a meaningful headed or visual surface exists, expose the active test session rather than hiding all verification in background logs. For web work, open the built-in browser or headed browser view and visibly show navigation, clicks, form input, assertions, screenshots, console and network evidence, and pass/fail progression when supported. For Swift and other native work, show the appropriate live preview, hot-reload surface, simulator, emulator, device stream, application window, interaction trace, screenshots, and relevant logs when available and permitted. Users may collapse, detach, background, or leave a visible test session while automation continues; the system preserves session state and does not require the user to watch every action. When a live surface cannot be embedded, expose an Open or Watch action, snapshots, screenshot sequence, video

items.title: Users can change session presentation without stopping automation

dimension_assessments.summary: Default testing, override truthfulness, discovery, installation, capability modes, and visible-session behavior are explicit.
The core names broad research, installation, browser, GUI, device, accessibility, performance, security, and evidence capabilities.
Override and provenance inputs and visible evidence outputs are named, but exact schemas, redaction outcomes, and session-state payloads are incomplete.
Core contracts exist for override, capability settings, provenance, and redaction, but snapshot and redaction-failure contracts are incomplete.
Auto, On, Off and presentation-state behavior are named, while authority denial, rollback failure, snapshot mutation, and restored session transitions remain open.
User approval and privileged-action authority are required, but mandatory blocker behavior and authority-resolution details are not deterministic.
Automated_Testing_System is the owner and cross-owner implementation surfaces are explicitly named.
Planning Wizard, Plan Compile, Executor, Orchestrator, GUI, permissions, and evidence consumers are named, but cross-surface dependency order is not encoded.
Settings and visible-session GUI truth is substantial, but visibility eligibility and restored presentation-state behavior are ambiguous.
Safe points, receipts, revalidation, rollback, and blockers are named; rollback failure, denied authority, and redaction failure states are not specified.
Pre-display and pre-persistence redaction is mandatory, but failure detection, quarantine, and fail-closed behavior are absent.
An effective policy snapshot propagates to four consumers, but its revision, freeze, invalidation, and dependency semantics are unspecified.
Discovery, installation, receipts, safe points, revalidation, rollback, visible presentation, and fallbacks are operationally described, but failure procedures and runtime oracles are incomplete.
Performance testing is a configurable family, but no latency, evidence-volume, retention, concurrency, streaming, or resource-budget oracle constrains this system.
Global-to-project inheritance is defined, but migration and compatibility behavior for preexisting settings, tools, receipts, or changed capability taxonomies is absent.
Truthful exception and compile-lineage oracles exist, while runtime, security, GUI continuity, rollback, and performance oracles do not.
Consequential discretion remains in research selection, authority denial, policy snapshot timing, visibility qualification, session restoration, redaction failure, and runtime test thresholds.
The review found material unknowns in selection, snapshot lifecycle, failure transitions, visibility predicates, persistence, redaction disposition, compatibility, and executable validation.
